title: Favorite pianists, including Yancey
summary: He explains his own piano influences and names Jimmy Yancey as his favorite; both men praise Yancey's simplicity.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And then who is your own personal favorite, influences?

Well, I guess, what it most sounds like is probably like Elton Bonner. But it's not that he's my favorite piano player. It's just that I think it fits in good with the band I play. And it's simply, I think it's the style that I can come closer to. True, I don't have the good technique. And he don't have the good technique either, I think.
Who would you name as your favorite piano player?
James B. You like him, huh?
James B. Johnson. Is that who you mean? No, no, I mean Jimmy Jansen. Jansen.
Play on his own, yeah. You know who he's Jansen. Oh, Yancy! Yeah, yeah.
Yeah, I think he's great. But I mean I couldn't play that in the band. No, you couldn't just play blues.
I love him because he's so simple.
But nobody can play like him. It's so easy.
It's so much machine if you try to play like him. Yeah.

Well, he had that time and that feeling and that touch. If you don't have that you've just lost everything. It's so amazing that anybody could play that simple and get so much music out of it. He just had so much inside of him I guess it comes out. Since you've been in New Orleans, well what happened when you came to New Orleans? I'll put it that way. You came alone?
